One-sentence judgment: a school bus driver is not "taking students from point A to point B," but picking up and dropping off students at fixed points on a strict schedule, being responsible for student safety while boarding, alighting, and riding, and maintaining order in the cabin. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET-SOC 53-3051.00, which O*NET lists as Job Zone 1-2 (preparation from little to some, SVP below 6.0), and Bright Outlook is not marked. The core boundary is: you may independently complete pre-departure vehicle and safety equipment inspections, run the approved route and schedule, apply boarding, alighting, and crossing safety rules, maintain order, and report faults and accidents; but you may not change the approved route and stops on your own, may not carry students beyond capacity, and may not drive a school bus without holding a school bus driving qualification.

Signals to keep exploring: your interest in "delivering a busload of students safely and on time with good order" is greater than in "whether the route is new," and you are willing to repeatedly execute the same route per a strict schedule and safety rules; you can stay calm and adhere to procedures amid noisy students, complex road conditions, and parent communication pressure; you accept split morning and afternoon schedules and seasonal arrangements and are willing to learn first aid basics and emergency handling.

Conditions for pausing high-cost investment first: you have not yet, while holding the driving license for the corresponding vehicle class and having obtained the school bus driving qualification, completed under mentoring or supervision a full closed loop from pre-departure inspection, on-schedule pickup and drop-off, boarding, alighting, and crossing safety execution, order maintenance, and anomaly reporting, to end-of-shift records; or you are unwilling to manage students per safety rules and cannot accept split schedules and seasonal arrangements; also, do not treat "can drive a car or an ordinary bus" as proof that you can drive a school bus.

Education, qualifications, and authorization must be verified separately: O*NET lists this occupation's preparation level as Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), usually requiring a high school diploma or equivalent or GED, with on-the-job training from a few days to a year; in the United States, school bus drivers usually need the school bus and passenger endorsements on a commercial driver's license (CDL) and must meet driving record, medical examination, and vision and hearing requirements, and usually pass a background check; in mainland China, school bus drivers shall obtain the school bus driving qualification under the Regulations on the Safety Management of School Buses: hold the driving license for the corresponding vehicle class with more than 3 years of driving experience, be at least 25 and no older than 60, have no record of a full 12 points in the most recent 3 consecutive scoring cycles, have no liability record for a traffic accident causing death or serious injury, have no drink-driving or drunk-driving record and no record of serious traffic violations such as overloading or speeding in passenger transport within the most recent 1 year, have no criminal record, and have the public security traffic management department endorse the motor vehicle driving license to permit driving a school bus.

One sentence: this is a position centered on safe student transport, cabin order maintenance, vehicle and safety equipment inspection, anomaly reporting, and operating records, and its outputs are reviewable driving and report records and safely completed student transport service; it is not a role that decides routes and fees on its own, nor does it replace the school bus safety management responsibility of the school and the competent department. The U.S. wage, employment, and projection data use this occupation's basis, Bus Drivers, School (SOC 53-3051); for mainland China, the evidence routing does not publish occupation-level or proxy wage figures for this occupation, keeping only the statistical basis and the gap.

The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, safe transport and vehicle inspection (checking tires, brakes, wipers, lights, oil, water, and safety equipment before departure, picking up and dropping off at fixed points on a strict schedule, obeying traffic laws and driving safely and courteously, and performing minor repairs when needed); second, student care and cabin order (applying boarding, alighting, and crossing safety rules, escorting young students across the road, maintaining order in the cabin, reporting student misconduct to school administrators, and adjusting heating, lighting, and ventilation for comfort); third, records, reporting, and emergency response (preparing and submitting reports on student counts or trips, work hours, mileage, and fuel consumption, reporting vehicle faults and items needing repair, reporting delays and accidents, and maintaining first aid procedure knowledge and handling emergencies). All three share the same work chain centered on student safety and reviewable records.
Safe transport and vehicle inspection

Inspect the vehicle and safety equipment before departure → pick up students at fixed points on a strict schedule → obey traffic laws and drive safely and courteously → transport students in sequence among neighborhoods, schools, and school activities → drop students off in sequence on arrival and confirm handover → record mileage, fuel consumption, and trips after the shift and report faults for repair.
Student care and cabin order

U.S. O*NET includes escorting young students across the road, maintaining order, and service tasks; actual pickup and drop-off in China are carried out per the division between the driver and the on-board attendant throughout the trip. Articles 38—39 of the Chinese regulation require an on-board attendant throughout the trip, responsible for guiding order beside the vehicle, counting students and confirming safe seating and belting and signaling departure after the door is closed, stopping dangerous behavior, and verifying that all students have left the vehicle on alighting. Drivers inspect the safety and technical condition of the vehicle per Article 41 and are prohibited from departing with hidden hazards; schools and service providers bear system, education, and maintenance duties per 10—12/22, and all student care or permits cannot be attributed to the individual driver.

Prepare and submit reports containing student counts or trips, work hours, mileage, or fuel consumption, report delays and accidents by telephone or mobile two-way radio, record the school bus route, keep the cabin interior clean, and maintain first aid procedure knowledge in order to provide aid in emergencies.

School bus drivers produce student transport operated per safety rules; transit and intercity bus drivers serve ordinary passengers on passenger transport routes, with different service objects and shift patterns; shuttle and limousine drivers serve hotel, airport, and corporate transfers; taxi drivers operate on meter per passenger instructions, generally not on fixed routes and schedules; school bus monitors supervise students on board and maintain order but do not drive the vehicle; crossing guards and flaggers control passage around schools and do not bear vehicle driving and in-cabin safety responsibility; transit and railroad police and emergency medical technicians bear enforcement or medical duties with completely different qualifications and responsibility boundaries. Similar names or working in the same transport and campus safety settings do not mean qualifications and responsibility boundaries are interchangeable.
Core purpose

Implement pickup and drop-off, inspection records, and anomaly reporting per applicable driving and student safety rules, supporting safety and punctuality; schools, service providers, and attendants collaborate per their own duties.
Main objects and basis

The objects are school buses and their student passengers, established pickup and drop-off points, approved routes, and school schedule arrangements; the basis is road traffic safety law and vehicle class requirements, school bus safety law and operating safety rules, the school's pickup, drop-off, and order management requirements, vehicle inspection and driving record systems, and first aid procedures and emergency handling requirements (in mainland China also the provisions of the Regulations on the Safety Management of School Buses concerning school bus use permits, school bus driving qualifications, and on-board attendants).
Core process

Pre-departure vehicle and safety equipment inspection, pickup and drop-off at fixed points per the schedule, boarding, alighting, and crossing safety execution, cabin order maintenance, anomaly and emergency handling, reporting and records, and end-of-shift handover of vehicle condition.
Main outputs

Student transport service completed per the school calendar and schedule, complete and reviewable driving and operating reports (student counts or trips, work hours, mileage, fuel consumption), vehicle fault and repair reports, delay and accident report records, and handling records of maintaining safety rules and order.
Responsible parties

Articles 38—39 of the Chinese regulation require an on-board attendant throughout the trip, responsible for guiding order beside the vehicle, counting students and confirming safe seating and belting and signaling departure after the door is closed, stopping dangerous behavior, and verifying that all students have left the vehicle on alighting. Drivers inspect the safety and technical condition of the vehicle per Article 41 and are prohibited from departing with hidden hazards; schools and service providers bear system, education, and maintenance duties per 10—12/22, and all student care or permits cannot be attributed to the individual driver.
Authority and approval

Article 30 of the regulation provides exceptions where the approved route is affected by traffic control, construction, disasters, severe weather, or major accidents; Article 22 requires suspension of operation and repair when safety conditions are not met. Under Article 42, at an accident the driver and attendant immediately call the police and set up warnings; if students remaining in the vehicle are in danger, the attendant evacuates them to a safe area and makes contact. Protect and report per the actual emergency procedures, and do not wait for approval of an ordinary route change before handling danger. China's school bus regulation 23—26: the corresponding driving license and at least 3 years of driving experience, age 25—60, no full points in 3 consecutive scoring cycles, no liability for a traffic accident causing death or serious injury, no drink-driving or drunk driving, no serious violations such as passenger overloading or speeding in the most recent 1 year, no criminal record, and compliance with health conditions and no alcoholism or drug use; the school bus driving qualification is obtained through public security traffic endorsement and is reviewed annually. The commercial passenger transport age of 63 cannot replace the school bus age.
Conclusion boundary

The driving and operating records state "what transport this pickup and drop-off run completed per plan and what anomalies occurred"; they do not equal a determination of accident responsibility, nor do they replace the school bus safety management judgment of the school and the competent department, and they will change with review and subsequent handling.

Before onboarding, verify at least six items: the position basis and form of employment (school-operated, school bus service company, or outsourcing), shift and schedule arrangements (including split morning and afternoon periods, the class timetable, and the school calendar), vehicle class and school bus driving qualification requirements, whether the approved route and pickup and drop-off points are fixed, safety and emergency handling training arrangements (including first aid and evacuation), and the real pay method (hours, trips, or semester-based, and the allowance basis).
Occupational basis

The 2022 Classification Code 4-02-02-01 passenger vehicle driver covers driving motor vehicles to provide passenger transport services, including but not limited to bus and transit drivers and also taxi and ride-hailing drivers, which is a broader related detailed class and does not equal the dedicated U.S. school bus scope 53-3051. The absence of a separately listed school bus title does not imply that China has no related driving detailed class; the specific employment identity and the statutory school bus qualification are verified separately. O*NET2025: education services 51%, transportation and warehousing 36%, government 11%, and other 2%. The OOH school bus section separately details local elementary and secondary schools 48%, school and employee bus transportation 34%, local government (excluding education and hospitals) 11%, and private elementary and secondary schools 2%, which are not exactly the same combined basis; Chinese industries are not inferred from U.S. shares.
Education and training pathway

O*NET new-entrant education Q&A: 59% high school or equivalent, 37% less than high school, and 3% postsecondary certificate, not the education of practitioners. JobZone1—2/SVP below 6 as a preparation range is a general summary; the BLS typical entry for this occupation is a high school diploma / None related experience / short-term on-the-job training, which does not equal several days to one year for every individual. The U.S. CDL is verified by vehicle threshold and state, and transporting the corresponding students to and from school or school activities uses the P/S endorsements; initial licenses or endorsements require separate verification of ELDT and exceptions. China's school bus regulation 23—26: the corresponding driving license and at least 3 years of driving experience, age 25—60, no full points in 3 consecutive scoring cycles, no liability for a traffic accident causing death or serious injury, no drink-driving or drunk driving, no serious violations such as passenger overloading or speeding in the most recent 1 year, no criminal record, and compliance with health conditions and no alcoholism or drug use; the school bus driving qualification is obtained through public security traffic endorsement and is reviewed annually. The commercial passenger transport age of 63 cannot replace the school bus age.
Methods and tools

The detailed profile's 3 software categories are browsers, map creation (AOL MapQuest), and operating systems; the Hot list has 1 specific product, Windows, with hiring percentages NA rather than 0. Categories, products, hiring mentions, and actual deployment or AI adoption are different. School bus equipment and repair are verified against actual safety specifications and permits.
Safety and work permits

Work risks mainly involve long periods of sitting and repetitive motion, an enclosed cabin and contaminant exposure, very hot or very cold environments, traffic risk when students board, alight, and cross, student behavioral conflicts, and the consequences of traffic accidents and emergencies; O*NET work context shows 93% work inside an enclosed vehicle every day, 80% need to make decisions every day, 59% sit continuously or almost continuously, 80% use their hands to handle objects and tools continuously or almost continuously, 36% are exposed to contaminants daily, 66% face time pressure or strict deadlines every day, 46% report very high responsibility for the health and safety of others, and 74% are on a regular schedule; pre-departure inspections should be completed per procedures, driving should follow the school bus driving qualification and operating rules, boarding, alighting, and crossing safety rules should be applied, and safety equipment used and emergency training attended as required.
Training and regulatory requirements

China's school bus regulation 23—26: the corresponding driving license and at least 3 years of driving experience, age 25—60, no full points in 3 consecutive scoring cycles, no liability for a traffic accident causing death or serious injury, no drink-driving or drunk driving, no serious violations such as passenger overloading or speeding in the most recent 1 year, no criminal record, and compliance with health conditions and no alcoholism or drug use; the school bus driving qualification is obtained through public security traffic endorsement and is reviewed annually. The commercial passenger transport age of 63 cannot replace the school bus age. The school bus use permit is applied for by the school or service provider per 14—15 and differs from the driver's individual qualification.
Pay and working hours

The OOH notes that part-time work and the school calendar limit working hours; O*NET74% regular / 14% seasonal / 13% irregular is Q&A. Editorially verify wages, split morning and afternoon periods, holidays, trip allowances, and certification costs; no uniform pay frequency was verified.

School bus drivers (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 53-3051.00, Bus Drivers, School) drive school buses to transport students, ensure adherence to safety rules, and may assist students in boarding or exiting; the official description is "Drive a school bus to transport students. Ensure adherence to safety rules. May assist students in boarding or exiting." Daily work includes: obeying traffic laws and driving safely and courteously; applying safety rules when students board or alight or cross near school bus stops; checking the condition of tires, brakes, wipers, lights, oil, fuel, water, and safety equipment and confirming everything is serviceable; reporting vehicle faults or items needing repair; picking up and dropping off students at fixed neighborhood points on a strict schedule; escorting young students across the road; driving gasoline-, diesel-, or electric-powered multi-passenger vehicles to transport students among neighborhoods, schools, and school activities; maintaining student order during the trip to ensure safety; maintaining first aid procedure knowledge; preparing and submitting reports containing student counts or trips, work hours, mileage, or fuel consumption; reporting delays, accidents, or other traffic and transport situations by telephone or mobile two-way radio; recording the school bus route; keeping the cabin interior clean; reading maps and following written and oral geographic directions; adjusting heating, lighting, and ventilation systems for student comfort; reporting student misconduct to school administrators; and performing minor repairs on the vehicle. It bears student safety transport and riding service responsibility, but does not replace the school bus safety management responsibility of the school and the competent department. This task list is a U.S. group; minor repair is Supplemental and does not authorize Chinese drivers to bypass school bus repair enterprise qualifications or replace the on-board attendant.

paragraphs:
Workplace | 93% of respondents work inside an enclosed vehicle every day; 23% work indoors not in a controlled environment every day.
Contact and communication | 67% are in constant contact with others and 21% have contact most of the time; 61% have face-to-face discussions every day; dealing with external customers or the public is extremely important to 33%.
Posture and physical effort | 59% sit continuously or almost continuously and 28% sit more than half the time; 80% use their hands to handle objects and tools continuously or almost continuously; 46% perform repetitive motions continuously or almost continuously.
Exposure and environment | 36% are exposed to contaminants daily; 18% are exposed to very hot or very cold environments daily; 38% are in very hot or very cold environments at least once a week.
Decision and accuracy | 80% need to make decisions every day; 44% say being exact or accurate is extremely important and 34% say it is very important; 66% face time pressure or strict deadlines every day.
Result impact | 46% report very high responsibility for the health and safety of others; 12% report very high responsibility for the work results of other staff and 24% report high responsibility.
Conflict and emotion | 12% deal with unpleasant, angry, or discourteous people every day and 21% at least once a week; 32% encounter conflict situations at least once a week.
Work arrangement | 74% are on a regular schedule (established routine, fixed timetable); 14% are seasonal (only during certain periods of the year) and 13% irregular; 51% say their work involves no competition at all.
Standing and walking | 70% stand less than half the time and 27% never stand; 68% walk or run less than half the time and 29% never; 52% never kneel, crouch, bend, or crawl.
51% rate the consequences of error as extremely serious; 20% over 40h per week / 76% under 40h is Q&A, not lawful hours; the percentages are not risk rates or position permits.

paragraphs: This page compares school bus drivers with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference better suits. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupation descriptions, and do not mean trade names are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 53-3051.00 and the adjacent entries (U.S. basis); the vehicle class, qualifications, and safety requirements of adjacent trades must be verified separately under their own jurisdictions, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares the directional differences between school bus drivers and adjacent trades; the basis for judgment is the main outputs, the objects of responsibility, and the qualifications required, rather than the similarity of trade names.

Emergency medical technicians center on medical first aid and transport and need the corresponding medical qualifications; this occupation centers on transporting students per schedule and applying safety rules and does not bear medical treatment duties.
If you prefer medical first aid, examine emergency medical technicians first; if you prefer student transport and safety order maintenance, examine this occupation first.
Provide on-site first aid and transport for acute and trauma patients, with outputs mainly first aid handling records and patient handover.
Emergency Medical Technicians

Parking enforcement workers have enforcement duties and corresponding authorization and do not drive transport vehicles; this occupation centers on driving the school bus and student safety and reports violations per procedures.
If you prefer enforcement and order management, examine parking enforcement workers first; if you prefer driving a school bus and caring for students, examine this occupation first.
Patrol parking order, issue citations, and handle illegal parking, with outputs mainly enforcement records and citations.
Parking Enforcement Workers

Transit and railroad police have enforcement duties and corresponding qualification requirements and do not perform school bus transport tasks; this occupation centers on driving and student boarding and alighting safety.
If you prefer enforcement and safety patrol work, examine transit and railroad police first; if you prefer school bus driving and student care, examine this occupation first.
Enforce the law, patrol, and handle safety incidents within the transport system, with outputs mainly enforcement and incident handling records.
Transit and Railroad Police

Crossing guards and flaggers are only responsible for on-site passage control and do not drive vehicles or bear in-cabin student safety responsibility; this occupation bears driving, cabin order, and student care responsibility at the same time.
If you prefer on-site passage control without driving responsibility, examine crossing guards and flaggers first; if you prefer driving and caring for students, examine this occupation first.
Control passage around schools and construction sections and guide students or pedestrians across, with outputs mainly on-site passage control.
Crossing Guards and Flaggers

School bus monitors do not drive the vehicle and focus on student supervision and order; this occupation centers on driving and vehicle safety equipment inspection and bears driving safety responsibility.
If you prefer care and order management without driving responsibility, examine school bus monitors first; if you prefer driving a school bus, examine this occupation first.
Supervise students on board, assist with boarding and alighting, and maintain order, with outputs mainly safe student escort and order maintenance.
School Bus Monitors

Transit and intercity bus drivers serve ordinary passengers on passenger transport routes, with different service objects and route forms; this occupation serves the student group and must apply boarding, alighting, and crossing safety rules and bear student supervision support duties.

If you prefer running urban or intercity passenger routes, examine transit and intercity bus drivers first; if you prefer transporting students and arranging schedules per the school calendar, examine this occupation first.
Carry ordinary passengers per passenger routes and schedules and collect fares, with outputs mainly passenger service and fare and driving records.
Bus Drivers, Transit and Intercity

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main outputs, the objects of responsibility, and the qualifications required, not how similar the names are; once the direction is set, you should verify item by item the target position's vehicle class and qualification requirements, shift and schedule arrangements, service objects and route scope, and training and certification arrangements, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

Before holding personal driving and school bus qualifications, first run non-operational walkthroughs of public or fictional routes, inspections, and reports; on-vehicle training follows the conditions of a lawful institution, and real pickup and drop-off must meet personal qualifications, permits, and arrangements, and mentoring cannot replace qualifications, nor may students be used as practice objects.
School bus drivers already on the job

Editorial tool pilot: route queries, inspection records, ledgers, and reports can assist; distinguish the duties of drivers, attendants, schools, and service providers by jurisdiction, and do not attribute all Chinese boarding, alighting, and emergency care to the driver. Articles 38—39 of the Chinese regulation require an on-board attendant throughout the trip, responsible for guiding order beside the vehicle, counting students and confirming safe seating and belting and signaling departure after the door is closed, stopping dangerous behavior, and verifying that all students have left the vehicle on alighting. Drivers inspect the safety and technical condition of the vehicle per Article 41 and are prohibited from departing with hidden hazards; schools and service providers bear system, education, and maintenance duties per 10—12/22, and all student care or permits cannot be attributed to the individual driver.
School and school bus service management teams

Editorially suggest verifying system authority, data, and review responsibility; drivers, attendants, and school service providers each handle matters per their duties, and the attendant may lawfully stop unsafe operation, so the driver is not given sole final say over all on-site decisions.
Education and development

Focus training on safe and defensive driving, student boarding, alighting, and crossing safety rules, riding order and behavior guidance, vehicle and safety equipment inspection, first aid procedures and emergency evacuation, and driving and operating report standards, while also training the awareness of verifying system prompts and monitoring data and the habit of proactively reporting doubtful points.

paragraphs: Boundary: this section describes occupational risk and responsibility boundaries, not an evaluation of any individual or institution; specific procedures and handling processes are determined by the applicable jurisdiction, institutional rules, and work authorization.

Risk clues include prolonged sitting, repetitive motion, contaminants and cold or heat, student boarding and alighting, vehicle hazards, and incident handling. Context percentages are not incidence rates; drivers, attendants, schools, and service providers divide duties per the regulations, and posture and data verification are separate editorial suggestions.

U.S. O*NET tasks and context provide occupational clues; China's school bus regulation sets qualifications, use permits, inspection, and the division of care and emergency duties. Employment projections are not used as risk evidence; health posture, authority, and debriefs are editorial suggestions and do not claim risk intervention effects.
School bus drivers
Long periods of sitting and repetitive motion, an enclosed cabin and contaminant exposure, and very hot or very cold environments may harm health.

Editorially verify seating, rest, ventilation, and actual hygiene requirements; the health qualification conditions under regulation 23 and the annual review under 26 are implemented per actual procedures, and the posture suggestions are not called verified disease prevention.
Driving continuously without rest to meet the schedule, ignoring physical discomfort, or departing while ill.
Drivers, attendants throughout the trip, and schools or service providers
Traffic risk during student boarding, alighting, and crossing may cause personal injury, and the consequences of error are extremely serious.

Articles 38—39 of the Chinese regulation require an on-board attendant throughout the trip, responsible for guiding order beside the vehicle, counting students and confirming safe seating and belting and signaling departure after the door is closed, stopping dangerous behavior, and verifying that all students have left the vehicle on alighting. Drivers inspect the safety and technical condition of the vehicle per Article 41 and are prohibited from departing with hidden hazards; schools and service providers bear system, education, and maintenance duties per 10—12/22, and all student care or permits cannot be attributed to the individual driver. Stopping and signal arrangements follow 32—33, and the U.S. escort task does not authorize a Chinese driver to leave the driving position.
Releasing students early to save time, picking up or dropping off at non-approved points, or starting without confirming safety.
Drivers, on-board attendants, and schools or service providers
Improper handling of student behavior and order conflicts may cause personal injury and parent disputes.

Under 39, the attendant maintains student boarding and alighting and in-cabin order and stops dangerous behavior; the driver keeps driving safely and cooperates and reports promptly. Accidents follow the division under 42, and if students remaining in the vehicle are in danger the attendant evacuates them and makes contact.
Escalating an argument with a student on board, or handling student behavior on your own without reporting.
School bus drivers and the fleet
Missing a vehicle or safety equipment inspection may leave a school bus operating while defective and directly endanger student safety.

Under regulation 41, check brakes, steering, lighting, tires, the safety door, seats, and seat belts before departure and do not drive a school bus with hidden hazards; under 22, suspend operation and repair when safety conditions are not met, with repair by a correspondingly qualified repair enterprise, and driver experience does not permit self-repair.
Omitting inspection items on experience, or taking a chance on a fault warning and continuing to depart.
Schools and data management positions
Leakage of student and parent information, pickup and drop-off arrangements, and operating data may lead to compliance and privacy consequences.

Editorial data suggestion: handle student and parent materials per the unit's actual authority and platform authorization; no dedicated data law compliance or NIST basis was obtained for this page, and an occupational classification publication source cannot serve as a data security law.
Taking student rosters and family information out of the workplace or disclosing them to unrelated persons.
Qualification and compliance positions
Driving without the school bus driving qualification or beyond the approved scope will cause safety and legal risk.

China's school bus regulation 23—26: the corresponding driving license and more than 3 years of driving experience, age 25—60, no full points in 3 consecutive scoring cycles, no liability for a traffic accident causing death or serious injury, no drink-driving or drunk driving, no serious violations such as passenger overloading or speeding in the most recent 1 year, no criminal record, and compliance with health conditions and no alcoholism or drug use; the school bus driving qualification is obtained through public security traffic endorsement and is reviewed annually. The commercial passenger transport age of 63 cannot replace the school bus age. Use permits, passenger capacity, and routes are verified separately under 14—16/30/34 and are not automatically obtained by passing training.
Driving a school bus while the qualification has expired or is not endorsed, or treating another person's qualification or ordinary driving experience as proof of one's own qualification.

Stop and verify uncertain vehicle conditions, student situations, or handling methods first, rather than skipping steps on experience.

If a practice step requires contact with real road operations, passenger-carrying driving, or student care, stop and mark that step as one that must be performed by personnel with the corresponding qualifications.

Record each deviation the reviewer points out and your subsequent revisions to form a reviewable improvement record.

entries.answer: Drive a school bus to transport students and operate per the school timetable: inspect tires, brakes, wipers, lights, oil, fuel, water, and safety equipment before departure, pick up and drop off students at fixed neighborhood points on a strict schedule, apply safety rules when students board or alight or cross near stops and escort young students across the road, transport students among neighborhoods, schools, and school activities, maintain cabin order and report student misconduct to school administrators when necessary, adjust heating, lighting, and ventilation, prepare and submit reports on student counts or trips and work hours and mileage and fuel consumption, record the school bus route, report vehicle faults and items needing repair, report delays and accidents, keep the cabin clean and maintain first aid procedure knowledge, and perform minor repairs on the vehicle.

entries.answer: Risks to note in advance include occupational health problems from long periods of sitting and repetitive motion, an enclosed cabin and contaminant exposure, very hot or very cold environments, traffic risk when students board, alight, and cross, student behavior and order conflicts, and the consequences of traffic accidents and emergencies; control depends on safe and defensive driving training, pre-departure vehicle and safety equipment inspection, strict application of boarding, alighting, and crossing safety rules, handling and escalating order and emergencies per procedures, and driving and operating records and debriefs.

entries.answer: A fit signal is maintaining compliant operation over the long term under fixed routes and a strict schedule, insisting on applying student boarding, alighting, and crossing safety rules, handling and reporting per procedures when student order is abnormal, and recording counts and mileage truthfully; liking to drive alone is not enough to prove competence.
